clue.text: Angry about a famous huntsman mostly requiring one to give way

definitions.note: a phrase describing the noun: a major road is one that requires traffic joining it to give way

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for angry is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: mad means angry
taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the famous name loses its tail end

parts.note: John Jorrocks is the hunting grocer of R. S. Surtees' comic novels

explanation.surface: A furious rider, nearly a famous master of hounds, has to make way for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Jorrocks is the comic hunting grocer of Surtees' novels. Araucaria's 'mostly' is generous: three letters go, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: At a junction traffic from the minor road must yield, so the main route is the one that makes others stop and wait.

clue.text: With see-through material, it's hard to be a prophet

parts.note: mica is a mineral that splits into transparent sheets
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone complains how difficult it is to foretell the future with a window of clear stuff in front of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Micah is one of the twelve minor prophets of the Hebrew Bible, with a book bearing his name.

clue.text: Traffic not moving? Let off steam and it's a piece of cake

parts.note: a traffic jam is stationary traffic
a steam engine puffs as it lets off steam

explanation.surface: Stuck in a hold-up, a driver vents frustration, and the situation is described as easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cake' looks like the idiom for something easy, but here it is literal: a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam puff is a flaky pastry filled with jam, literally a small piece of confectionery.

clue.text: Travel to capital, say

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the city name and hear another word

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital, here reached by travelling to it

explanation.surface: A traveller heads for a major city.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander about widely, a form of travelling without fixed route.

clue.text: Alternative unknowns: this is an antelope

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
algebra uses x and y for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A maths problem with two unknown values turns out to describe a horned animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is a large African and Arabian antelope with long straight horns.

clue.text: Belittling of a good interchange

indicators.note: the second half of the long word is read on its own as an order to rearrange what precedes it

parts.note: a good plus the first half of interchange is the fodder; the second half is the signal

explanation.surface: Someone disparages a fine motorway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'interchange' is split: 'inter' is fodder and 'change' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogation means disparagement, speaking of something as less worthy than it is.

clue.text: Little fool on the plus side?

definitions.note: a phrase describing the noun: an asset sits on the credit side of a balance sheet

parts.note: an ass is a fool
-et is a diminutive suffix, as in owlet and islet

explanation.surface: A small idiot, looked at optimistically.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'little ass' made with the diminutive ending, like owl to owlet, gives ASS-ET.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounting, possessions of value are listed in the credit column, so an item of value counts in your favour.

clue.text: Trouble on-line about doctor, a fool, giving instructions

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the trouble word goes round what follows

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
MO is a medical officer
a nit is a fool
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Online strife involving a doctor and an idiot leads to someone issuing orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-line' is read as two words: the trouble word sits on top of the abbreviation for railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Admonitory means warning or reproving, conveying advice on how one ought to behave.

clue.text: Attack the arrangement continuously

parts.note: a set-up is an arrangement
on as in carrying on without stopping

explanation.surface: An order to keep assaulting an arrangement without pause.
explanation.definitionFit: To set upon someone is to assault them suddenly, a phrasal verb for an assault.

clue.text: Triumvirate you need time to look up in a book

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word for a book

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to see is to look
HR is short for hour

explanation.surface: To trace the history of three joint rulers you must find a moment to consult a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumvirate is a ruling group of three people, so it is a trio or group of three.

clue.text: Businessman takes stewed fruit right round an American walkway

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the fruit dish goes round the following words

parts.note: compote is fruit stewed in syrup
taken as written
Y is Yankee in the radio alphabet, and a Yankee is an American
a prom is a promenade, a seaside walkway
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A trader carries a pudding of stewed fruit around a US boardwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the fruit dish goes round; the letter for right is tacked on at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: A company promoter is a person who sets up and launches new commercial firms, so a kind of entrepreneur.

clue.text: Drag the swag

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pull something heavy
second meaning: a thief's take of stolen goods

explanation.surface: Burglars heave away their loot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for hauling something heavy and a noun for a thief's booty.

clue.text: Silver for a boy, endless fount of inspiration

indicators.note: endless means the word for a boy loses its final letter

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written
a nipper is a small boy

explanation.surface: A silver gift for a lad turns out to be an unending source of creativity.
explanation.walkthrough: Aganippe is the spring on Mount Helicon sacred to the Muses, whose water inspired poets.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Muses' spring gave poetic inspiration to those who drank, so it is literally a source of it.

clue.text: Liberal by letter?

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A question whether a political liberal communicates by post.
explanation.definitionFit: Permissive means tolerant and allowing freedom, which is what liberal means as an adjective.

clue.text: Suitor with unit adapted to be good for him

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters of the two words are refashioned

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wooer working alongside a team is changed into the right man for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good for him' suggests a suitable match; here it means healthy to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutritious food provides nourishment and benefits the health of whoever eats it.

clue.text: Ransack barrel to find a piece of weaponry

parts.note: to rifle is to search through thoroughly
a butt is a large cask

explanation.surface: Someone tips out a cask looking for a hidden gun part.
explanation.definitionFit: The butt is the shoulder end of a gun's stock, a component of a firearm.

clue.text: Bird giving offence during firework noise

indicators.note: during means within, so the offence word sits inside
noise points to a sound, so the firework is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a rocket is a firework, written as it sounds
to give someone the pip is to cause offence or irritation

explanation.surface: A bird takes umbrage when fireworks go off.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock pipit is a small brown songbird of rocky coasts in Britain and Europe.

clue.text: Sunburn dispenser? It takes 2

parts.note: a tan is skin browned by the sun
read cryptically, a dispenser of sunburn is what makes it go

explanation.surface: A tube of after-sun lotion needs two people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the saying 'it takes two to tango', meaning a joint enterprise needs both partners.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine ballroom dance is performed by a couple, as the proverb about needing two partners says.

clue.text: Little boy with a metre-wide hole

parts.note: Chas is a short form of Charles
M is the symbol for one metre

explanation.surface: A small child stands beside a gap a metre across.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm is a deep fissure or gorge in the ground, a large gaping opening.

clue.text: Stuffy and far from 'irsute

parts.note: far from hirsute is bald; the apostrophe shows the H dropped in speech

explanation.surface: A stuffy room and a bald man described in a dropped-aitch accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'irsute marks a dropped H, Cockney style, so the opposite of hairy loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy room lacks fresh ventilation, being close and without circulating breeze.

clue.text: Organ playing during journey out of Mexico

definitions.note: a phrase for the noun: the river flowing along and out of Mexico's border

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the rearranged letters go inside

parts.note: a ride is a journey

indicators.note: playing suggests a musician improvising, so the instrument's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Music played on a trip as one leaves Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the Rio Grande forms Mexico's northern border and runs out to the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river along the US frontier is the natural way out of Mexico to the north.

clue.text: Modern way to get into prison

parts.note: new means modern
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A new method of getting into jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was London's notorious prison until 1902.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate is the historic London gaol that stood beside the Old Bailey courts.

clue.text: Hanger-on at location of Red Devils?

parts.note: the Red Devils are the Parachute Regiment's display team, paratroops
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Asks whether a hanger-on is found where Manchester United's Red Devils play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Devils' suggests Manchester United; here it is the British Army's parachute team.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off another; a hanger-on clings to someone for gain, as a sponger.

clue.text: Lubber employed at the theatre

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a clumsy, lubberly sailor, a swabber
second meaning: a pad used in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A clumsy oaf gets a job at the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a clumsy seaman and a pad of absorbent material surgeons use.

clue.text: Man of law, not yet man to the French

parts.note: a boy is a male not yet grown
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A lawyer, not yet a man, speaks to the French.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Boyle gave his name to Boyle's Law of gases, so the 'law' is physics, not the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyle formulated the gas law relating pressure and volume, so his name is attached to a scientific principle.

clue.text: Light wood?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ray of light
second meaning: a long piece of timber

explanation.walkthrough: 'Light wood' reads as balsa or pine; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a shaft of radiance and a heavy horizontal timber in building.

clue.text: Attempt crazy rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: bats means mad

explanation.surface: A mad attempt to get up.
explanation.definitionFit: Have a stab at something means to try it, so the noun is a try or go.

clue.text: With student and petty officer separated in prison, I can do anything

indicators.note: separated in says the two items go into the prison word at different points

parts.note: a penitentiary is a prison
PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer
L is a learner

explanation.surface: With a student and a naval officer locked up apart, a prisoner boasts of unlimited ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separated' means the two insertions go in at different places in the prison word, not side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenipotentiary is an envoy given full powers to act on behalf of a government, a speaker with authority for anything.

clue.text: Smack in the snoot, as technically it is known

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the comma
surface padding completing the phrase about technical terms

explanation.surface: A punch on the nose, described in technical language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like a blow; here it means a flavour, as in 'smacks of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a slight flavour or trace of something, which is what taste means.

clue.text: Note: see about part of speech I'm withdrawing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so see wraps around the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: withdrawing means going back, so those words are written backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a verb is a part of speech

explanation.surface: A speaker retracts part of what they said.
explanation.definitionFit: A semibreve is the whole note in music, the longest commonly used note value.
